title: Cohomology comparison for ordinary pullbacks of the specified affine Cech model
statement: Let $f:X\to T$ be separated [def-pc-morphism-conventions], $F$ a quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module, $U\subseteq T$ an affine open and $V:\operatorname{Fin}(r)\to (f^{-1}U).\mathrm{Opens}$ a covering by affine opens. Put $p=f|_U$ and $G=F|_{f^{-1}U}$. For every cartesian square with base map $g:T^{\prime}\to U$, projection $g^{\prime}:X^{\prime}\to X$ and $f^{\prime}:X^{\prime}\to T^{\prime}$, assuming injective resolutions in $X^{\prime}.\mathrm{Modules}$, and every $q\in\mathbb N$, there is an isomorphism $H^q(g^*C(p,G,V))\cong R^qf^{\prime}_*(g^{\prime})^*F$ of $\mathcal O_{T^{\prime}}$-modules, where the explicit complex is [def-pc-finite-affine-cech-model]. No relative flatness is assumed; tensor is applied to the complex before taking homology.

proof.text: Define the pulled-back opens Wi=gprime inverse image jY(Vi), indexed by ULift Fin r. Their supremum is top: image and inverse image commute with supremums, the original family covers Y, and the cartesian commutativity equation ensures gprime takes every point into Y. Obtain the same D, epsilon, e and differential descriptions together with local scalar compatibility from the linear Cech resolution.

For each full tuple y, its old intersection Z is affine by separatedness of Y over the affine U. Its pulled-back intersection equals gprime inverse image jY(Z), since the image under an injective open immersion commutes with nonempty finite intersections. The proved intersection lemma makes both its inclusion and its map to Tprime affine. Affine higher-image vanishing and the open-pushforward composition comparison show each factor j_*(M|W) is fprime_*-acyclic. Acyclicity is invariant under isomorphism and finite products, so every D term is acyclic. The affine acyclicity proof is reproduced in private proved helpers from CechAcyclicOnAffines and rightAcyclic_of_epi_map_g, rather than importing DirectImage.AffineMorphism: that module imports proper finiteness through FiniteFreeComplex and closes an import cycle back to this comparison. Injective modules are flasque, this Cech-acyclic class is closed under the indicated cokernels, and the affine preimages of affine base opens give sectionwise surjectivity, hence epimorphisms after pushforward. Dimension shifting then supplies the required acyclicity.

Apply the section-complex base-change comparison to this D, e, hd and local scalar formula. It identifies the homology of the specified pulled-back model with the homology of fprime_*D. The already proved generic acyclic-resolution criterion rightDerivedObjIsoOfResolution identifies the latter with higherDirectImage fprime q applied to M, since epsilon is a quasi-isomorphism and pushforward is left exact. Compose the two actual isomorphisms. This works for every supplied square and every q, including the empty cover.

theorem finiteAffineCechModel_comparison {X T : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ T)
    [IsSeparated f] (F : X.Modules) [F.IsQuasicoherent]
    (U : T.Opens) (hU : IsAffineOpen U) {r : ℕ}
    (V : Fin r → (f ⁻¹ᵁ U).toScheme.Opens) (hV : ∀ i, IsAffineOpen (V i))
    (hcover : iSup V = ⊤) :
    ∀ {T' X' : Scheme.{u}} (g : T' ⟶ U.toScheme) (g' : X' ⟶ X) (f' : X' ⟶ T')
      [HasInjectiveResolutions X'.Modules], IsPullback g' f' f (g ≫ U.ι) → ∀ q : ℕ,
      Nonempty ((((Modules.pullback g).mapHomologicalComplex _).obj
          (finiteAffineCechModel (f ∣_ U) (F.restrict (f ⁻¹ᵁ U).ι) V)).homology q ≅
        (higherDirectImage f' q).obj ((Modules.pullback g').obj F))
